channel.title: The Idaho Stack
channel.description: Idaho technology news, business, infrastructure, and practical reporting.

item.title: Before Micron Day, Check the Route From CWI Classes to a Paid Job
item.description: CWI’s October 20 event comes just before spring registration. Its catalog and Micron’s hiring rules show why a certificate, a class start and a paid apprenticeship need separate plans.

item.title: Four Providers Withdrew From Idaho’s Broadband Plan. What Happens to Those Locations?
item.description: An October state briefing documents a broadband rebid after provider withdrawals. Here is how Idaho households can check project status without mistaking an award for service.

item.title: Idaho’s Broadband Money Is Leaving the Map Phase. Now the Hard Part Starts.
item.description: Idaho’s $583 million BEAD broadband program has moved from awards and maps into contracts, permitting, construction schedules, and accountability deadlines.

item.title: The Data Center Question Idaho Hasn’t Settled: Who Pays for the Power?
item.description: Idaho Power is planning for fast load growth as Micron, Meta, and future large users enter the system. The unsettled question is who carries the cost and risk.

item.title: What Idaho’s Tech Economy Is Actually Made Of
item.description: Idaho’s technology economy is not apps first. It is memory chips, nuclear labs, broadband buildout, irrigation systems, manufacturing fixes, and small businesses trying to make AI useful.

item.title: Idaho Tech Briefing: What We’re Tracking First
item.description: Micron, INL, broadband, water, small-business AI, repair culture, and the workforce questions underneath it all.

item.title: Why Idaho Matters More to American Technology Than Most People Think
item.description: Idaho is not trying to be Silicon Valley. Its technology story is more physical: chips, reactors, farms, broadband, repair, and the small businesses where new tools either work or fail.

item.title: Micron, Memory, and Idaho’s Place in the Chip Supply Chain
item.description: An archive analysis of Idaho’s place in the memory-chip supply chain. The page displays an updated date; its original publication time has not been verified.
